title: Use several cases
summary: A table of cases checks the same rule with several inputs. Keep each expected result easy to see.
introduction: A table of cases checks the same rule with several inputs. Keep each expected result easy to see. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A table of cases checks the same rule with several inputs. Keep each expected result easy to see.

blocks.code:
const cases = [[0, 0], [2, 4], [-3, -6]];
for (const [input, expected] of cases) console.log(input * 2 === expected);
blocks.title: Use several cases

blocks.text: Three true values are printed. The cases include zero, a positive number and a negative number.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: More repeated cases do not help if they all test the same uninteresting path.
For more detail later, use this [Unit Testing further reading](https://nodejs.org/api/test.html).
